newsitem.title: USA: Unimarc up in New York debut.
newsitem.headline: Unimarc up in New York debut.

text.p: Chilean retailer Supermercados Unimarc SA rose in its New York debut Friday, boosted by optimism about its prospects and Chilean growth.
The American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were up 1-1/8 to 17-7/8, easing slightly from its opening jump to 18. Volume in early afternoon was almost 720,000 ADRs.
A trader said Unimarc had been helped in part by concerns about Chile's leading supermarket chain, Santa Isabel SA, and its strains from expansion into Peru and Paraguay.
Unimarc, Chile's No. 3 chain, "has been taking market share from them. They are a good little company," he said. "The stock's doing pretty well."
Alberto Montagne, a retail analyst at Lehman Brothers, said Unimarc, like other Chilean retailers, was needing capital to expand.

"There will be a relatively large investment this year in that sector, supermarkets and malls and all those other retail outlets," he said, adding that retail investment could reach more than $2 billion this year.
Montagne said retail sales were expected to grow six percent this year and eight percent in 1998. That growth will be helped by lower unemployment and higher real wages.
Investors' sentiment on Chile remained strong and Unimarc "sounds like a well-run company and an interesting management turnaround story," said Mark de Speville, a retail analyst at Robert Fleming.
De Speville added that he had not talked with company managment and was concerned about analysts' differing estimates for earnings this year and next. Those figures were not immediately available.
Unimarc also carried out an initial public offering in Santiago. The shares were at 150 pesos in mid afternoon.
